rationale: This is essentially a mechanical double-sort of two canonical published anomalies (Sloan working-capital accruals and Novy-Marx gross profitability) and is conceptually very close to the archived WorkingCapital-Accrual/Margin composite, so it offers little incremental insight even though the expression and sign are internally coherent.

The conditional logic is internally consistent and economically sensible (receivables build is only alarming when cash conversion is weak), but the oancf/sale leg is close to Ball et al.'s cash-based operating profitability and may dominate the interaction, so the test should include a horse race against that leg alone.

A genuinely conditional refinement rather than a rediscovery — inventory growth is known, but sharpening it on deteriorating gross margin is a defensible markdown/demand-softness mechanism — with sign and expression correctly aligned, though the 3-period TREND is short and invch coverage should be checked.

The two accrual legs in the SUMRANK are highly collinear so the blend adds little, and RE/AT trend is largely a restatement of retained profitability, making this a third near-duplicate of the accruals-times-profitability composite already covered by the archive and Proposal 1.

The quality leg (high mean ROA plus low ROA volatility measured over only three observations) is both a known profitability/earnings-stability anomaly and statistically fragile at that window length, so the modestly novel tax-accrual-noise idea is likely swamped by a noisy, already-published component with weak txach coverage.

The opacity-times-leverage mechanism is the most original proposal here and the sign matches the expression, but the leverage leg has a historically ambiguous (often positively-priced-then-reversed) return relation and the absolute-value accrual measures depend on sparsely populated cash-flow items, so coverage and leg-level diagnostics are essential.
